text.text_excerpt: I'm a big fan of Chef Sue Zemanick and have been wanting to try this new spot since it opened. I finally took the opportunity this week. The space is small but lovely. I was actually surprised that the layout was still very standard dinner since I expected something more wine bar in the space. The wine by the glass has interesting selections; I had a couple of glasses of a lovely sparkling rose since that's a perfect August refreshment. I was pleased to see they have a full bar too. The small plates we sampled were delicious and perfect. We had: tuna tartare...bright and beautiful with the seaweed salad ceviche...very interesting and delicious but after the tuna a bit more mundane roasted...

IVY has replaced Vizard's, a local fine dining place that I still love to this day. It was a successful and delicious fine dining restaurant until the owner's made a personal decision to close the doors. Now that Ivy has replaced one of our favorite restaurants, we had to try it and see if it was worthy of the location... With the weather cooling down South, dining outside was perfect! I felt the inside was a bit stuffy and that night they had some too-cool-for-me type elevator music. The food? DE. LISH. The menu is divided into small plate portions, which are perfect for sharing. Of course, each small plate is good to share between two, so order accordingly. One notable dish was the Warm...

My admiration Sue Zemanick is no secret, so my expectations for the food at Ivy were very high...but apparently, not high enough. When we first learned that Ivy was in the planning stages, we were told it would be competing with the Bouligny Tavern/Delachaise style wine/cocktail bars that served food. While I love those places, the cuisine at Ivy blows them out of the water. My lovely wife and I joined some friends for a snack & drinks meet up, but the food and attentive, warm service made our experience more of an event.
